topics.title: Region and the nation: the Indian approach and areas of tension
topics.ncert_sections: Region and the Nation; Indian approach; Areas of tension

concepts.learning_objective: Explain how the Indian approach balances unity and diversity and treats regional aspirations democratically.
Identify the major regional tensions India faced in the first decades after Independence.

topics.title: Jammu and Kashmir
topics.ncert_sections: Jammu and Kashmir; Roots of the Problem; External and internal disputes; Politics since 1948; Insurgency and After; 2002 and Beyond

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the circumstances of Jammu and Kashmir's accession and the idea of Kashmiriyat.
Distinguish the opposite reactions to the special status of Jammu and Kashmir under Article 370.
Trace the political developments in Jammu and Kashmir from 1948 to 2019 and explain the rise of insurgency.
Explain the aims and democratic methods of the Dravidian movement and the DMK's early agitations.
Evaluate how Dravidian parties show the compatibility of regionalism and nationalism.

topics.title: Punjab
topics.ncert_sections: Punjab; Political context; Cycle of violence; Road to peace

concepts.learning_objective: Explain the political context of Akali politics and the Anandpur Sahib Resolution.
Describe Operation Blue Star, the assassination of Indira Gandhi and the anti-Sikh violence of 1984.
Identify the provisions of the Punjab Accord and analyse how peace returned to Punjab.

topics.title: The North-East: autonomy and secession
topics.ncert_sections: The North-East; Demands for autonomy; Secessionist movements

concepts.learning_objective: Describe the features of the North-East region and its political reorganisation.
Explain how autonomy demands in the North-East were accommodated within the constitutional framework.
Compare the secessionist movements in Mizoram and Nagaland and their outcomes.

topics.title: Movements against outsiders and the Assam Movement

concepts.learning_objective: Explain why migration into the North-East led to movements against 'outsiders'.
Analyse the causes, methods and outcome of the Assam Movement and the Assam Accord of 1985.

topics.title: Accommodation and national integration
topics.ncert_sections: Accommodation and National Integration; Sikkim's merger (box); Goa's liberation (box)

concepts.learning_objective: Evaluate the lessons the chapter draws for accommodating regional aspirations in a democracy.
Describe how Sikkim and Goa became part of the Indian Union.
